route: /style-board/ (the style board: module table:cards, longest and shortest copy, photos as grey frames; no competitor section shows this module)

findings.issue: The ten cards are solid navy (#0b2a4a) on a white section, which makes a heavy dark wall the competitor never puts on a white ground.
findings.reference: On white or beige grounds the competitor's cards are outlined: 1px solid black or #979797, radius 6–10px, no fill and no shadow, with dark text (components.md, three outlined cards and channel cards). It saves navy for whole sections such as MOQs and Selecting colours.
findings.fix: In reference.css, give .block--table .table-card a transparent background, a 1px solid #979797 border and border-radius: var(--radius-card), and set color and --heading-color back to var(--text-primary). Set .table-card__row dt to var(--text-muted) and change the row rule to a dark hairline.

findings.issue: The card titles (Certifications, Fabrics, Lead times…) are set at 1.0625rem in a regular weight, so they barely stand out from the body text under them and the cards lose their hierarchy.
findings.reference: The competitor's card titles are Maison 700, clearly bolder than the text below them (outlined cards: card title 700 22px/33px).
findings.fix: In reference.css, set .block--table .table-card__title to font-weight: 700 with line-height 1.3, using the hero/heading family as the FAQ h3 does (line 302). Do not copy the 22px size; only the weight changes.

findings.issue: At 390 px the card title ('Design and samples', 'Samples and fees') is the same size and weight as the body text, so in a long single column of 10 tall navy cards nothing marks where each card's subject starts.
findings.reference: The competitor's card titles are bold (700) and stand clearly above their text on phones too.
findings.fix: Use the same .block--table .table-card__title font-weight: 700 rule (not limited to one width) together with the outlined-card treatment, so the column reads as light cards with bold titles.

findings.issue: Each of the 10 cards repeats the same muted column label 'What this means for you' above its text, and this repeated label is the only row in the card.
findings.reference: The competitor's cards carry a title and their text, with no repeated field label.
findings.fix: In TableBlock.astro's cards layout, when the table has only one data column, leave out the dt label (or make it visually hidden) and render the cell as the card's paragraph.
